seamModel.description: The synthetic `__omnimuxComposerFiles[sessionId]` stub implements the async bridge contract: `async add(files)` records each File name/type/size, reads `file.text()`, mounts a synthetic native file card and updates `list()` synchronously on success before resolving `{ok:true}` (or resolves `{ok:false,message}` in the busy probe); the module awaits the Promise. The real tray has a VOID official `onAddFiles(files): void` intake; it shows its own toast for a rejected batch and returns nothing, so the hub bridge confirms success by observing the official attachments list (bounded 1500ms) and keeps an unconfirmed name in list() for a 3s TTL after a timeout so an immediate retry deduplicates instead of uploading twice. That confirmation/TTL logic, the tray registration and the silent-failure fallback are covered by the 16 hub bridge/hook tests, not by this fixture; the stub does not simulate the TTL.
seamModel.noPrefillSeam: window.__omnimuxSessionPrefill is not installed; the module no longer writes the draft or calls the prefill seam.

assertions.name: click opens the collapsed conversation through 3 no-arg ensure calls, without the collapse/focus fallback
exactly one native Markdown file is handed to the official composer intake
Markdown content carries the collection facts, member ids and inspiration_get instruction, without a question line
the composer draft is untouched, no send/prefill happens, the reveal-attachments bridge is used and no toast appears
second click on the same collection is deduplicated by list() and explains why with the attachment-exists toast
add() failure surfaces the official localized rejection message and creates no attachment card
missing native bridge falls back to the unavailable toast after the bounded wait, without touching the draft
no browser request escaped the fixture origin; no console exceptions

boundaries: Synthetic native-files bridge + workbench ensure stub + composer/card DOM; this is not a full Host install. The real AttachmentTray registration and delegation to the official onAddFiles/upload lifecycle are covered by hub bridge/mount tests; official upload and Dev visual acceptance are human-owned.
Real: product InspirationSection bundle, production local handlers/store, real loopback HTTP, real File generation in the page and real DOM writes in headless Chrome.

The Markdown document lists all three fixture members (qa-dance1/qa-dance2/qa-fashion1); the task text mentioned two member ids as examples, the assertion covers every member in the fixture collection.
No Dev app (port 45120), no user profile, no external network; dynamic loopback ports only; Chrome/server/temp store cleaned up.
